scout.documented_relatives:
Sources: Wikidata links in and out of Batman (Q2695156) via P941 'inspired by', P144 'based on' and P4969 'derivative work'; influence sentences in the Batman, Bob Kane, Bill Finger, Detective Comics #27 and related articles; and Wikipedia full-text search for 23 derivative phrases ('pastiche of Batman', 'Marvel's Batman', 'parody of Batman' and so on). The curated list has 36 entries, 30 of them with a verbatim evidence sentence saved. Strength grades: A = a creator statement or Wikidata link plus Wikipedia text; B = a Wikipedia text claim; C = a comparison or review remark only.

INFLUENCES (Batman drew on them):
- Zorro (A). Kane credited The Mark of Zorro (1920); Wikidata P941.
- The Bat (A). The 1920 Rinehart and Hopwood play, its 1926 film (DEV) and The Bat Whispers (1930), which Kane names in Batman and Me.
- The Shadow (A). Wikidata P941; the first Batman story is derived from the Shadow pulp 'Partners of Peril'.
- Sherlock Holmes (A). Wikidata P941; named in the Batman article.
- Doc Savage (B) and Dick Tracy (B). Named in the Batman article, through Finger.
- Lee Falk's The Phantom (B). Finger and Kane cite it for the white eye lenses.
- The Black Bat pulp (B). Wrist gauntlets; no work with a plot section.
- The Man Who Laughs, 1928 film and Hugo novel (A). The Joker's look.
- Robin Hood (B). Robin's name.
- Superman (A). Wikidata, plus the Detective Comics #27 brief.
- Count Dracula (C). Wikidata only.

PREDECESSOR: the Scarlet Pimpernel (B). The Batman article names the Pimpernel and Zorro as predecessors; the Pimpernel article lists Batman among its followers; the Zorro article calls Sir Percy Zorro's direct literary predecessor.

DERIVATIVES:
- Moon Knight (A): Wikidata, 'Marvel's Batman', and a 'pastiche of Batman' criticism.
- Nighthawk, Marvel (A): based on Batman in the Squadron Sinister.
- Nite Owl II of Watchmen (A): Wikidata P144; parodies Batman.
- Midnighter (B): a Batman analogue and pastiche.
- Riggan Thomson of Birdman (A): Wikidata P144.
- Blue Falcon (A), Darkwing (A), Knight Watchman, Professor Night, Mermaid Man, Rat-Man and Confessor: Wikidata P941.
- Iron Man (B): Bob Layton based the armours on Batman's specialised outfits; Stan Lee modelled Tony Stark on Howard Hughes.
- The Wild World of Batwoman (B), Rat Pfink a Boo Boo (B), Bluntman in the Jay and Silent Bob films (B), Blackwolf in Soon I Will Be Invincible (B), Commander Courage (B; plot too short), Superhero Movie (C).
- Black Panther (C): Priest's concept was partly inspired by Batman.

SIBLINGS (a shared documented ancestor):
- Darkman (B): Raimi wanted The Shadow, and reviewers compared the film to Batman.
- Puss in Boots of Shrek (B): modelled on Banderas's Zorro.

UNVERIFIED: The Count of Monte Cristo. The brief names it, but I found no Wikipedia or Wikidata statement linking it to Batman.

RECLASSIFIED: 'Chase Me' (Wikidata P144) is a 2003 Batman animated short, so it belongs to the Batman lineage, not to the derivatives.

ELIGIBLE TEST WORKS: 52 works not in DEV with at least 8 plot sentences; 34 are already in the T3 category pool and 18 are not (586 sentences). Those 18:
- The Bat (play), The Bat Whispers, The Bat (1959)
- The Sign of the Four, The Hound of the Baskervilles, The Valley of Fear
- Dick Tracy (1990 and 1945)
- The Man Who Laughs (1928 film and the novel)
- 'Pimpernel' Smith
- Watchmen (comic), Birdman, Jay and Silent Bob Strike Back, Scooby-Doo! Mask of the Blue Falcon
- Puss in Boots (2011), Puss in Boots: The Last Wish
- John Wick: Chapter 3

Relatives covered by eligible works: 9 of 12 influences, the predecessor, 9 of 14 derivatives, both siblings, all 3 named book tier-1 members and 3 of 5 tier-2 members (Angel is a TV character; Daredevil's film is in DEV). Too short or missing: The Mark of Zorro (1920, 6 sentences), The Curse of Capistrano (no plot section), the Moon Knight series (TV). Many derivatives are comic or TV characters with no film.

scout.book_family:
Mike Taylor's earlier book, pp. 21-22:
- The 'billionaire vigilante orphans' are four: Batman, Iron Man (which the book calls Marvel's response to Batman), and before them Zorro and the Scarlet Pimpernel.
- A wider group of 'memetically similar' orphan vigilantes who are not necessarily billionaires: Spider-Man, Daredevil, John Wick, Angel (from Buffy the Vampire Slayer) and Puss in Boots.
- The book also gives a copying chain: Orczy (Pimpernel) to McCulley (Zorro) to Finger (Batman) to Stan Lee (Iron Man).
- p. 12 has the pitches 'Batman is Zorro in Manhattan' and 'Iron Man is Batman in California'.

The design brief lists Puss in Boots in the core family, but the book places it in the wider tier.

DEV already holds several family works as cousins: the Puss in Boots folktale, the Scarlet Pimpernel novel, The Mark of Zorro (1940), Iron Man (2008), Spider-Man (2002) and Daredevil (2003). The T3 prediction therefore has to use other works, all of which are in the pool or relatives files:
- Zorro: The Mask of Zorro, The Legend of Zorro, the 1975 Italian Zorro and 15 more Zorro-category works
- Pimpernel: the 1934 and 1982 films, The Return of the Scarlet Pimpernel, Eldorado, The Elusive Pimpernel (novel), 'Pimpernel' Smith
- Iron Man: Iron Man 2, Iron Man 3, Rise of Technovore
- Tier 2: the Spider-Man and John Wick sequels, Puss in Boots (2011) and The Last Wish

I quote only short phrases from the book here.

LLM READING, made-up 24-sentence story of about 500 tokens. Qwen3-8B and Llama 3.1 8B 4-bit, mlx-lm, peak memory about 5.4 GB:
- Prompt processing about 1,300 to 1,470 tokens per second; generation about 60 tokens per second.
- Yes/no judge with no cache: 0.42 s per meme.
- With the story prefix cached: 0.36 s to process the story once, then 0.12 s per meme, so 3.3 to 3.4 s for 25 memes.

- Flat 80-word summary: 2.5 s. Two-level recursive summary: 6.1 to 6.7 s.

That is about 13 times faster than extract.py's 3,700 sentences per 12 minutes, which is limited by fp16 memmap writes and the int8 re-quantisation pass. The per-work aggregate is 1.8 MB in fp16.

scout.language:
All checks used made-up sentences only; no corpus text and no activations were analysed. I wrote the translations myself, as Claude agents would for TEST.

TOKEN COST relative to English, same three sentences (Qwen / Llama):
- zh 0.96 / 1.28
- es 1.53 / 1.53
- fr 1.54 / 1.55
- ja 1.58 / 1.54
- ru 1.63 / 1.49
- de 1.70 / 1.68
- th 1.89 / 1.75
- hi 5.21 / 2.96

Every language round-trips through decoding and maps correctly onto extract.py's sentence spans. The name placeholders X1 and X3 tokenise as 'X' plus a digit in every script.

COMPREHENSION, 24-sentence made-up story, six detail questions answered in English (my own scoring):
- Qwen: English 6/6, Chinese about 5/6 (missed that the mother's death was deliberate), Spanish about 5.5/6.
- Llama: English 6/6, Chinese 5/6 (got the merchant's escape wrong), Spanish 6/6 (Spanish words leak into its English answers).
- Earlier scout: Qwen back-translated zh, ja, ru and hi accurately. Llama just echoed the source text when the instruction came before the passage, but translated accurately and answered 3/3 questions when the instruction came after it.

RECOMMENDATION: Chinese as the main cross-language condition.
- It is the cheapest in tokens for both models (cheaper than English for Qwen).
- It shares no script with English, so lexical overlap with the English comics is zero and the test separates meaning from wording as far as possible.
- Both models understood it well here.
- Caveat: Chinese is not among Llama 3.1's officially supported languages (en, de, fr, it, pt, hi, es, th), though it worked in these checks.
- The justified alternative is Spanish, which both models support officially, at 1.53 times English. It shares the Latin script, cognates and some proper-noun tokens with English, so it is a 'near' condition. Adding it would give a graded far/near pair at about 2,900 more sentences.
- Hindi is too expensive for Qwen.

DESIGN NOTES:
- fetch_corpus.py's sentence splitter only works for English, so translate sentence by sentence and keep a 1:1 alignment.
- Chinese TF-IDF needs jieba or character n-grams.
- Keyword lineage is near zero across languages by construction. A fair keyword comparator needs translated keyword queries; the main vector rivals are e5 and LaBSE.
- Translate with Claude agents rather than either reader model, and check by back-translation with a second agent.
- Set presence bars on the translated baseline films.

Files (under <scratchpad>/prereg/scout/): lang_check_qwen3-8b.json, lang_check_llama3.1-8b.json, lang_check2_qwen3-8b.json, lang_check2_llama3.1-8b.json, lang_check3_qwen3-8b.json, lang_check3_llama3.1-8b.json. Scripts: lang_check.py, lang_check2.py, lang_check3.py.
scout.budget:
TEST SENTENCES PER MODEL:
- T1b drift: the 20 DEV screen works (13 films, 4 animations, 3 games; 644 name-free sentences) at 4 drift levels is 2,576 sentences. Drifting the 69 baseline films too, so the presence bars move with the drift, adds 9,068.
- T1c Chinese: 20 screen works plus 69 baselines is 2,911 sentences. Optional Spanish: another 2,911.
- T1d Shakespeare: 40 plays (1,438) plus 141 primary adaptations (3,689) is 5,127. Using all 177 eligible films gives 5,955.
- T2: about 25 memes times 80 items (20 held out in original wording, 20 paraphrased, 20 translated, 20 hard negatives), plus about 2,000 generic negatives: about 4,000.
- T2b: about 540 stories of about 25 sentences (120 base plots at 3 explicitness levels, 120 matched controls, 60 decoys): about 13,500.
- T3: 87,169 (52,100 without the vigilante-only works).
- T4, T5 and T6 reuse DEV.
- Total: about 115,000 to 126,000 sentences.

NEURON EXTRACTION per model:
- With extract.py (18,500 sentences per hour): 6.2 to 6.8 hours, or about 13 hours for both models.
- With a compact extractor that computes per-work aggregates on the GPU (measured at 68 sentences per second): about 30 minutes per model; T3 alone takes about 21 minutes.

STORAGE:
- Full per-sentence int8 activations: 0.885 MB per sentence for Qwen, 0.918 MB for Llama.
- Non-T3 sets (28,000 to 39,000 sentences): 25 to 36 GB per model, plus fp16 scratch twice that size while extracting, unless done in chunks.
- T3 in full would need about 157 GB for both models plus scratch. With 207 GB free it does not fit beside everything else, so T3 must store aggregates: 3,434 works times 1.8 MB is about 6.2 GB per model, plus about 1.7 GB per model of per-sentence int8 values for 20,000 selected units.
- Embeddings: about 0.4 to 0.5 GB per model.
- Everything together: about 70 to 85 GB.

COMPARATOR COMPUTE: all embeddings take under 10 minutes per encoder, and LSA, LDA and topic clustering take minutes.

LLM READING per local model (measured costs):
- T2b: judge with cached prefix about 31 minutes (no cache 95 minutes); recursive summaries about 1 hour plus about 30 minutes of judging. Neurons: about 3 minutes.
- T3, 30 memes: judge about 3.8 hours; recursive summaries about 7.6 hours.
- T1d pairwise source judgement (141 adaptations times 40 plays = 5,640 prompts): about 1.9 hours, or about 0.3 hours working from summaries.
- Batman drift and language lineage: about 15 minutes.
- Running every LLM rival on both models: roughly 25 to 30 GPU hours, against about 1 hour for neurons, embeddings and topics with the compact extractor.
- Cost picture per story: one neuron pass costs about the same as one LLM read of the story (0.36 s). The judge then adds 0.12 s per meme with caching. The neurons' cost advantage therefore grows with the number of memes and is small at 1 to 5 memes.

AGENT EFFORT (Claude), in calls:
- T1b drift: 80 rewrites, or 356 with drifted baselines, plus a plot-retention check for each. The realised word-replacement rate can be measured by script. About 160 to 712 calls.
- T1c: 89 texts per language translated sentence by sentence, plus back-translation checks: about 180 calls per language.
- T1d name removal in make_neutral style for about 217 texts: about 220 calls plus an audit.
- T2: meme set and examples about 25; paraphrases, translations and hard negatives about 75; 3 blind annotators over 4,000 items in batches of 50, about 240; keyword selection by LLM 25 per reader model (Qwen and Llama locally, Claude as upper bound).
- T2b: about 540 stories from at least 3 writer agents (about 180 to 540 calls) and 2 blind recognisability readers per story (about 360 to 1,080 calls).
- T6 blind label test: about 20 to 40 batched calls.
- Total: about 2,500 to 4,000 agent calls, dominated by T2b and T1b.

WALL CLOCK: Wikipedia fetching, now done, took about 1.5 hours for about 7,500 pages. The scout folder is 127 MB.

NOT DONE AND NEEDING MIKE'S APPROVAL: downloading the encoder weights (0.1 to 2.3 GB each) and installing bertopic, umap-learn, jieba and gensim.

I computed no outcome on any TEST text. I saved only metadata, counts and raw sections; the only reading of TEST plots was the requested check of which Shakespeare names appear. I changed no project files and wrote nothing under prereg/. I added a pause argument to the scratch helper wiki.py.

primary_hypotheses.hypothesis: Planted stories with the meme's usual words banned (reworded): a neuron unit picked from the meme's examples detects the meme better than an analyst's keyword search. The analyst's keywords are chosen by Qwen3-8B from the same label, definition and examples.
primary_hypotheses.test: T2. 24 memes; 120 new plots in 12 genres unrelated to Batman, each in 5 versions (explicit, banned, implicit, control, decoy), 600 stories. For each meme, the positives are its banned and implicit stories (about 30) and the negatives are every story without the meme (about 555). Statistic: mean over memes of AUC(neurons:qwen3-8b:m1) minus AUC(keywords:qwen3-8b). The unit is picked contrastively from the frozen examples against the 2,267 DEV reference-film sentences plus the other memes' examples. One-sided sign-flip over memes. Holm across H1 to H5 at 0.05.
primary_hypotheses.prediction: Mean AUC difference above 0. Power is 0.94 for a 0.10 gap.
primary_hypotheses.falsifier: Holm-adjusted p of 0.05 or more, or mean difference of 0 or less. Inconclusive if the Claude upper bound's reworded AUC is below 0.80, or the keyword AUC on explicit stories is below 0.75.

primary_hypotheses.hypothesis: On reworded stories, neurons are no more than 0.05 AUC worse than sentence embeddings (multilingual-e5-base prototype). If that holds, superiority is tested next in a fixed sequence.
primary_hypotheses.test: T2, same data. Statistic: mean over memes of AUC(neurons) minus AUC(emb:e5-base) plus 0.05; one-sided sign-flip, inside the Holm family. Superiority, the same statistic without the 0.05, is tested at H2's Holm threshold only if non-inferiority passes.
primary_hypotheses.prediction: Above 0 (non-inferior). No directional prediction for superiority.
primary_hypotheses.falsifier: Holm-adjusted p of 0.05 or more: neurons may then be more than 0.05 AUC worse than embeddings.

primary_hypotheses.hypothesis: The units already labelled on the DEV Batman corpus fire, unchanged, on their memes when those memes are planted in reworded form in new stories from unrelated genres.
primary_hypotheses.test: T2, the 18 memes that map to a DEV-labelled Qwen unit (dev_units.json). Statistic: mean over memes of AUC(devunit:qwen3-8b) minus 0.5 on reworded stories; one-sided sign-flip. Holm.
primary_hypotheses.prediction: Mean AUC above 0.5. Power is 0.80 at a mean AUC of 0.60.
primary_hypotheses.falsifier: Holm-adjusted p of 0.05 or more, or mean AUC of 0.5 or less. Same T2 inconclusive rules as H1.

primary_hypotheses.hypothesis: As a text's words are replaced (vocabulary drift with the plot kept), TF-IDF's recovery of the documented source degrades more than the neurons' does.
primary_hypotheses.test: T1b. Two lineages, each rewritten at 0, 25, 50, 75 and 100% of content-word types under drift_protocol.md, with the sources left unchanged. Batman: 16 targets (9 DEV adaptations plus 7 fresh animated adaptations) against 12 DEV comics. Shakespeare: 83 loose adaptations against 40 plays. Lineage share uses the E2 statistic (hub-adjusted, joint relabelling). Degradation is the mean share over levels 25 to 100 minus the share at level 0. Statistic: mean over 30 clusters (16 Batman targets and 14 source plays) of D_TFIDF minus D_neurons(Qwen); one-sided sign-flip. Holm.
primary_hypotheses.prediction: Above 0. Power is 0.85 for a 0.10 difference.
primary_hypotheses.falsifier: Holm-adjusted p of 0.05 or more, or a difference of 0 or less. Inconclusive if the realised removal of banned tokens at level 100 is below 90%, or if pooled TF-IDF is not worse at level 100 than at level 0.

primary_hypotheses.hypothesis: On a fresh lineage whose adaptations change names, setting and wording (loose Shakespeare film adaptations, names removed from all texts), neurons recover the documented source play better than TF-IDF does.
primary_hypotheses.test: T1d. 83 loose primary adaptations of 14 plays, ranked against all 40 plays. The hub is all 141 primary films adapting other plays; reference films are the DEV 69 minus The Lion King; the mean is play-weighted. Statistic: mean over plays of share(neurons:qwen3-8b) minus share(tfidf); one-sided exact sign-flip over the 14 plays. Holm.
primary_hypotheses.prediction: Below 0 (neurons recover the source better). Power is only 0.59 for a 0.08 difference and 0.90 for 0.12, so this is the weakest test.
primary_hypotheses.falsifier: Holm-adjusted p of 0.05 or more, or a difference of 0 or more. Inconclusive if TF-IDF fails the positive control on the original texts with names (share above 0.10).

draft.summary:
I've drafted the pre-registration in `preregistration/`. I computed no outcome on any TEST data and did not commit or push anything. The tests run on synthetic data: 62 checks, 0 failures.

**What it asks.** Every test compares the same methods on the same inputs: neurons (Qwen primary, Llama replication), keywords, sentence embeddings, LSA, topic models, the same model's hidden states, and LLM reading (judge, recursive summaries, pairwise lineage ratings), with Claude only as a labelled upper bound. Each test either changes the words on purpose (drift, Chinese translation, banned keywords) or uses a lineage where the words changed naturally (loose Shakespeare adaptations). Accuracy and cost are reported side by side.

**Primary hypotheses.** Five, all tested in Qwen with Holm correction across them at 0.05:
- **H1:** on stories with a meme's usual words banned, neurons beat an analyst's keyword search.
- **H2:** on the same stories, neurons are within 0.05 AUC of e5-base embeddings (then tested for being better).
- **H3:** the units already labelled on DEV fire on their memes when those memes are planted in reworded form in new genres.
- **H4:** as words are replaced, TF-IDF's recovery of the source degrades more than the neurons'.
- **H5:** on loose Shakespeare adaptations, neurons recover the source play better than TF-IDF.

Llama replicates a hypothesis if its p is below 0.05. Each primary has rules that make it inconclusive rather than falsified, and the code applies them when it gives its verdict. The 21 secondary predictions are corrected within each test family.

**What I changed from your candidate list:**
- **T2 and T2b merged** into one planted-story benchmark: 24 memes, 120 plots in 12 genres, 5 versions each (explicit, banned, implicit, control, decoy), with blind-reader quality checks. The Chinese and natural-text versions are secondary. Natural texts are annotated in full rather than pooled from method rankings, so no method biases the ground truth.
- **Drift test extended to the 83 loose Shakespeare adaptations.** With Batman alone (16 targets) H4 had only 0.61 power; with 30 clusters it has 0.85.
- **T1e added:** 7 new animated adaptations of DEV comics, as a positive control for the new-data pipeline and as extra drift targets.
- **T3 tests your book family on works not in DEV:** Zorro, Pimpernel and Iron Man films on the orphan-vigilante memes, against works in the same genre group. Documented relatives (19 entities, 56 works) are tested on Batman likeness with the generic-superhero part removed.
- **T4 extended to 75 Batman works.** Innovators are tested against shuffles that keep each work's position in the timeline, and survival against a neutral random-copying model.
- **T5 is now out-of-sample:** partners are chosen on DEV, and their correlation is measured on the new stories.
- **Spanish dropped.**

**Design fixes made while building:**
- The background sentences for picking units are processed exactly like the examples (one per document, same prefix), so units that respond to "second sentence of a document" can't win.
- The selection is contrastive: each meme's background also includes the other memes' examples. That stops units that only detect Claude's nameless writing style. The TF-IDF keyword query and the LDA topic choice use the same background.

**Built and checked:**
- **Compact neuron extractor:** matches the existing DEV scores at r = 0.99997 to 0.99998 in both models, about 0.7 s and 6.6 GB per work.
- **LLM judge, summaries, pairwise ratings and keyword choice:** smoke-tested on made-up stories.
- **Name masker for T3:** on DEV it hides 91% of the tokens the agent pipeline replaced, at 97% precision.
- **Work lists:** rebuild identically from the scout caches, with a hash of every Wikipedia text.

**Honest caveats in the document:**
- H1 is partly true by construction, since banned stories are written to defeat the usual keywords. The informative numbers are the size of the gap and how neurons compare with embeddings and LLM reading.
- Neurons are expected to cost about 13 times more than e5 embeddings, and less than the LLM judge at roughly one meme or more.
- H5 has the least power.

**Needs your approval before step 2:** installing sentence-transformers and umap-learn, and downloading the four encoders (about 5.3 GB). After that the run order is: push the pre-registration; run the DEV steps and push a DEV freeze (which must reproduce E2 within 0.03 of 0.164 and 0.102 before anything else); create the test data; push a test-data freeze; then run the analysis. Estimated cost: about 27 GPU-hours of LLM reading, about 35 minutes of neuron extraction per model, about 3,400 Claude agent calls, and about 60 GB of disk.

problems.problem: H4 (drift interaction) passes when the neurons recover nothing. D(t) = mean share at levels 25-100 minus share at level 0, and share is bounded below by 0 and pulled toward chance (about 0.47). A method that starts worse has less room to degrade. DEV already shows that the neurons start worse on the 9 DEV targets: per-target shares give Qwen 0.164 against TF-IDF 0.110, and TF-IDF has 6 of 9 targets at 0. So the statistic is not centred at 0 under the null that both methods are equally robust. I simulated this with analysis.signflip on 30 clusters, both methods losing the same proportion of their above-chance recovery (scratchpad review_sims/h4_floor.py). Starting from the DEV gap, H4 is 'supported' at p<.05 in 14% (moderate drift) to 43% (total loss) of runs. With neurons at 0.30 it passes in 81% to 100%. With neurons at chance at every level it passes in 100% of runs at p<.01. Because the DEV gap was known when H4 was written, a sceptic can say H4 was tilted in advance. test_analysis.py's H4 check ('d 0.086, p 0.0186') only shows that a planted effect is found. It never tests this null world.
problems.fix: Make H4's primary statistic a direct head-to-head under drift: the mean over clusters of [mean share over levels 50-100 for TF-IDF minus the same for neurons] > 0, with the level-0 difference reported beside it. Or define retention relative to each method's own permutation chance, rho_x(L) = (null_mean_x - share_x(L)) / (null_mean_x - share_x(0)), pooled within cluster so it is never divided by a near-zero margin. Also require the neurons' lineage test at levels 50 and above to be p<0.05 before H4 can be called supported. Add an equal-robustness null world, with neurons starting worse, to test_analysis.py and show the false-positive rate is at most alpha.

problems.problem: H1, H2 and H3 can be passed by a detector with no meme specificity. The negatives for meme m are its own control and decoy versions plus all 5 versions of the 105 plots without m. Only 315 of those 555 have any planted meme. The control fill is by protocol 'a neutral event', so planted and control versions also differ in how eventful and dramatic they are, not only in the meme. I scored a detector that fires on 'some listed element happened' identically for every meme, using analysis.detection_aucs on the real planted_design.json (review_sims/t2_eventfulness.py). Its mean reworded AUC is 0.56 to 0.68 (0.716 noiseless), and its hard-negative AUC is 0.66 to 0.92. H3's null of 0.5, and H1's comparison against keywords (which cannot pick up drama), would therefore be passed by a generic 'something dramatic happens' or 'death or violence' unit. Several DEV units (funeral, origin wound, revenge) are of that kind. Twin accuracy, T2-zh (non-specific AUC about 0.77) and T2-N (any Batman-ness unit beats 0.5 on every Batman meme) have the same flaw.
problems.fix: Make the primary T2 negatives salience-matched: the banned and implicit versions of plots that plant other memes but not m. A non-specific detector then scores 0.5 by construction. Report the current all-negatives and hard-negatives AUCs as secondary. Give H3, and the per-meme detector claims, a mismatched-meme null: each unit's AUC on its own meme's reworded positives minus its mean AUC on the other memes' reworded positives, tested by permuting meme labels across detectors. For new data, change the control instruction to 'an event of equal stakes and dramatic weight that is none of the 24 elements', and add a blind 1-5 salience rating of slot fills with a check that planted and control slots match.

problems.problem: H1 is close to true by construction. The primary keyword query is chosen by Qwen from the label (for example 'Secret identity') and 5 examples written in the meme's usual words, so it will largely reproduce the ban list (memes_for_tracing.json 'keywords'). Banned and implicit stories contain no ban-list word anywhere, so ban-list terms score 0 on every reworded positive. Meanwhile the same meme's decoys, which carry at least 2 of those words, sit in the negative set and score high. In my simulation a query that is a subset of the ban list gets a reworded AUC of 0.486. H1 therefore reduces to 'neurons exceed about 0.49', which the non-specific detector above already does. A sceptic will dismiss a positive H1 as a rigged comparison. The design admits that the banned condition was 'designed to defeat a meme's usual words' but still makes this comparison a primary test.
problems.fix: Make the primary keyword rival an evasion-aware analyst: the LLM is asked for 30 terms covering synonyms, euphemisms, slang and paraphrases (a moderation team's expanded lexicon), plus a WordNet or embedding-neighbour expansion of keywords:tfidf. Freeze it at F1. At F1, before any story exists, also compute and publish each query's share of terms that fall on the ban list. Remove the meme's own decoys from H1's negative set and test decoys separately under S11. Use the salience-matched negatives from the previous item.

problems.problem: A null on H1 or H3 would say little. The few-shot unit is chosen from 884,736 units using only 5 explicit-wording examples, so the selection rule systematically picks word detectors. The robustness review found the funeral unit correlates r 0.977 with the word 'funeral'. If H1 or H3 fail, nobody can tell whether units that track the idea exist but were not selected, or do not exist. Selecting a maximum over about 0.9M units with 5 examples also invites a winner's curse. Separately, the comparison is not 'identical tuning budget': the neurons search 0.9M candidates against a contrastive background, while the e5 and hidden-state prototypes are a plain mean of the examples with no background contrast.
problems.fix: Before F0, add 5 reworded examples per meme with no ban-list words to memes_for_tracing.json, written by a session that has not seen the stories. Pre-specify a neuron variant (m1-mixed) that selects on explicit plus reworded examples, and give every rival the same 10 examples: the embedding prototype, the keyword query and LDA. Give embeddings and hidden states the same contrastive supervision as the neurons: a fixed-regularisation logistic probe on examples against the contrastive background. That makes it a like-for-like 'learned detector' comparison.

problems.problem: The primary rivals are not the strongest ones DEV identified. On DEV name-free E2, LSA (0.064) beat TF-IDF (0.110), yet H4 and H5 compare the neurons only with TF-IDF. H2 compares only with e5-base, one of four encoders, and the promised best-encoder-in-hindsight sensitivity analysis is not implemented. A positive H4, H5 or H2-superiority result against the weaker rival is easy to dismiss.
problems.fix: Use an intersection-union rule: H4 and H5 are supported only if the neurons beat both TF-IDF and LSA, each one-sided at the Holm-assigned level (this needs no extra multiplicity correction). Claim H2 superiority only if the neurons beat both e5-base and e5-large. Alternatively, fix at F0 the DEV-best lexical and vector methods as the primary rivals.

problems.problem: 'Falsified' is claimed whenever the Holm-adjusted p is 0.05 or more, even for tests with low power. Stated power is H5 0.59 (0.29 at alpha .01) for a 0.08 difference and H2 0.77 (0.51). H4's assumed SD of 0.20 is optimistic: the per-cluster d is a difference of degradation differences, and with the DEV per-target SD of 0.22 and level correlations of 0 to 0.7 its SD is 0.13 to 0.25. Four of H5's 14 plays rest on a single film each (Two Gentlemen, Much Ado, Antony and Cleopatra, Love's Labour's Lost), so the per-play SD of 0.15 is optimistic for them. The section 6 promise that 'a null H5 will be reported as weak evidence' contradicts calling that same null 'falsified'.
problems.fix: Pre-specify a smallest effect size of interest for each hypothesis (for example 0.05 AUC for H1 to H3, 0.05 share for H4 and H5). Use a three-way verdict. 'Supported' means the Holm test rejects. 'Falsified' means the one-sided 95% bound excludes the smallest effect size of interest in the predicted direction. Anything else is 'undetermined'. Report power at the realistic Holm-adjusted alpha with SD 0.25 for H4, and per-play SDs that account for single-film plays.

problems.problem: The T1 lineage permutation null ignores the time rule. In analysis._shares, a relabelled 'source' (cmap[s]) can be a comic published after the target and is still used as 'best'. The robustness review already found that chance is overstated this way: 42 to 44% when time-consistent, or 39% era-matched, against 47%. Every Batman lineage p-value is therefore anti-conservative: T1a, the per-level T1b curves, S3 and S5 (Chinese), S7 (fresh adaptations) and the Batman 'beyond words' residual test.
problems.fix: In lineage_test, draw only time-consistent relabellings: rejection-sample permutations so every relabelled source is eligible for its target, or permute within publication-era blocks. Report null_mean against the honest 42 to 44%. Add a unit test showing the null mean matches the time-consistent chance.

problems.problem: The T3 tests S15 to S17 treat works within one character franchise as independent. stratified_perm_test shuffles individual works within a stratum, but the positives are franchise clusters: 18 Zorro, 8 Pimpernel and 17 Spider-Man works. A random set of works has a much narrower distribution than a set of near-duplicate sequels, so p is anti-conservative. Entity weighting changes the point estimate but not the null. S16 and S17 rest on 3 entities each (Zorro, Pimpernel, Iron Man; Spider-Man, John Wick, Puss in Boots), so they cannot test 'the book family' as a whole.
problems.fix: Use an entity-level null. Group the pool's negatives into franchises (Wikidata series or character, or title stem) and compare each positive entity's mean within-stratum percentile with same-size pseudo-franchises drawn from its stratum, the pseudo-franchise null the robustness review recommended. Report per-entity estimates with intervals, and state that S16 and S17 are claims about these 3 named characters each.

problems.problem: The T3 labels are contaminated and inconsistent. The 'pool' negatives, which also build the superhero centroid, include works where Batman or his supporting cast are major characters, for example Justice League (13 titles), Justice League vs. Teen Titans, the Teen Titans films (Robin), Birds of Prey, both Suicide Squad films and the Lego DC films. Same-entity works sit on both sides: Darkman is a relative but Darkman II and III are negatives; The Phantom (1996) is a relative but The Story of the Phantom is a negative; Dick Tracy films are relatives but Dick Tracy's Dilemma is a negative; 2 Robin Hood films are relatives while about 13 are negatives. The superhero centroid also includes each superhero negative itself. For noisy high-dimensional vectors such as neurons and TF-IDF, that inflates the negatives' superhero-likeness. After residualisation that lowers their Batman-specific score relative to the relatives, which biases S15 upward.
problems.fix: Assign roles at the entity level, so every work of a positive entity is a positive or is excluded. Using unmasked plot metadata, drop from the negatives any work whose plot names a Batman-family character (Batman, Bruce Wayne, Robin, Nightwing, Joker, Harley Quinn, Catwoman, Gotham, Alfred, Damian Wayne). That scouting is metadata-level, like the Shakespeare name check. Compute superhero-likeness with a leave-one-out centroid, or split the superhero negatives into a half that builds the centroid and a half that is tested.

problems.problem: analysis.py does not implement the document exactly, and section 0 says the code wins. Each gap below becomes an analysis written after the data are seen: (a) the rule dropping a meme that fails Q4 in more than 4 of 15 plots is not implemented in analysis.py or build_lists.py; (b) T2 results by writer and by tier are missing; (c) the best-encoder sensitivity is missing; (d) the H4 sensitivity without drift-flagged works is missing; (e) S1 (e5 against TF-IDF degradation) and S9 (summary judge against direct judge) are never computed, because secondary interactions are only rival against neurons; (f) S8 is computed two-sided although it is directional; S10, S11, S12, S13, S14 and S21 have no test or p-value, although BH q-values are promised; (g) no Cohen's kappa is computed anywhere for A1, A2 or the label test; (h) H3 has no 95% interval, although section 8 requires one; (i) plot_bootstrap_ci is defined but never used. test_analysis.py (0 failures, 62 checks; I re-ran it) checks only that planted effects are found. Apart from one draw each for the lineage and stratified nulls, it never checks the type-I error rate.
problems.fix: Implement every listed analysis before F0, each with a unit test. Add null-world tests to test_analysis.py: no effect in each of H1 to H5, an H4 world where both methods are equally robust and neurons start worse, a non-specific T2 detector world, and a franchise-clustered T3 world. Over at least 200 replicates, show that the rejection rate is at most alpha.

problems.problem: Forking paths stay open between F0 and F2. Section 10 lets changes be made after F0 if 'decided without TEST outcomes'. But F1 publishes DEV results for every rival (T1a) and the LLM keyword queries, so primary rivals, margins or hypotheses could still be changed after seeing how the comparators do on DEV. Also, features/ is gitignored and TEST features are never committed, so nobody can check that analysis.py was run once on frozen features.
problems.fix: Lock the hypotheses, primary methods, smallest effect sizes, negative sets and verdict rules at F0. Between F0 and F2, allow only logged bug fixes and feasibility changes. Add a freeze point F3: commit a manifest of sha256 hashes for every TEST feature file before running analysis.py, and log the first run's output hash.

problems.problem: The cost comparison is circular. The neuron pass is the same 8B model's forward pass as the judge's prefill: 0.36 s against 0.36 s on the timing run. So M* = (neuron s - prefill s) / per-meme s is about 0 by arithmetic, and 'cheaper than LLM reading above about 1 meme' is not a finding. One prefill could even produce both. Cost and accuracy have no pre-specified decision rule, although Mike wants 'how much more accurate, or cheaper' as the headline. One-off neuron costs are left out of the break-even: full activations for about 2,400 example and background sentences per model (about 0.9 MB per sentence) plus a search over 0.9M units per meme.
problems.fix: Pre-register a frontier rule: method A dominates B when A's accuracy CI lower bound is at least B's point estimate and A costs no more. Compare the neurons at matched cost against e5 (13 times cheaper per sentence, about 1.5 KB stored per sentence against 1.8 MB per work) and against a smaller LLM reader (for example Qwen3-1.7B or 0.6B) or a single prompt that answers all 24 memes at once. Include unit-selection and storage costs in the per-meme marginal cost, and report the cost of adding a new meme after extraction for each method.

problems.problem: T4 is circular, and S19 has no sharp falsifier. The extended lineage deliberately adds faithful animated adaptations of the predicted innovators: Year One (2011), The Dark Knight Returns (2012) and The Killing Joke (2016). It also already contains the DEV adaptations of those three comics (The Killing Joke alone has 4 adaptations, Year One 3). The trio's 'mutations' are therefore guaranteed to 'catch on'; S18 restates E2. For S19, the Bentley-style neutral model ignores two things: units differ in their base rates, and about 3% of presences are chance at the 2nd-of-69 bar. Real data will exceed a neutral copying model for any representation, words included, so beating the 95th percentile is not evidence of selection.
problems.fix: Measure a mutation's success only in later works that are not documented adaptations of the innovating work, and report it with and without the 7 fresh adaptations. Make S19 comparative, testing whether the neurons' excess over neutral is larger than that of words. Also use a null that keeps each unit's frequency, such as row- and column-margin-preserving swap randomisation of the work-by-unit matrix with the time order shuffled. Count a mutation only at a stricter presence bar, or after correcting for the chance presence rate.

problems.problem: S20 (T5 concept agreement) is computed on a held-out corpus enriched for the concepts. The 600 T2 stories were written to plant about 10 of the 27 concept labels (funeral, origin wound, joke, vat of chemicals, antidote, mantle, ward, secret identity, billionaire vigilante, corrupt police). The lexically matched null units were matched on DEV Batman text, whose words and names the stories ban or never use. So the concept units vary more than the nulls, and r(concept) - r(null) is inflated for reasons that have nothing to do with the two models agreeing.
problems.fix: Make the primary held-out corpus the 1,000 random films in the T3 pool. Per-sentence values for every T5 unit are already stored there through the frozen unit list. Report the T2 stories as secondary, and report per-concept variance ratios against the nulls.

problems.problem: The sign-flip tests assume independent clusters, which these are not. In H4, the Batman targets share the same 12 candidate comics and the same hub works, and several share a source (The Killing Joke for The Dark Knight, Batman '89, Joker 2019 and the 2016 film; Year One for Batman Begins, The Batman and the 2011 film), so correlated per-target d values make independent flips anti-conservative. In H1 to H3, inference is over memes only, with the 120 plots and 4 writers treated as fixed, so no interval reflects plot-to-plot or writer-to-writer variation. All 4 'independent' writers are Claude sessions.
problems.fix: In H4, cluster the Batman targets by documented source comic, or use a cluster bootstrap over source comics alongside the sign-flip. In T2, report a two-way (meme by plot) bootstrap interval and per-writer estimates, plus a leave-one-writer-out check of each primary result. State plainly that the benchmark measures memes as Claude writes them.

problems.problem: In T1c, the presence bars for the English comics are set on the Chinese-translated reference films. Units that respond to English text in general are then 'present' in all 12 comics, which is within the 2-16 band, and absent from every Chinese screen work. They flood the optional band, diluting containment and costing power, so a null S3 becomes hard to interpret.
problems.fix: Use language-matched bars: the comics' presence from the English name-free reference films, and the Chinese texts' presence from the Chinese reference films. Keep the optional band computed on those language-matched presences.

problems.problem: The lineage share counts a tie as not beating the source (strict '>' in _shares), which favours methods with coarse or saturated similarities. The LLM pair method's p_yes saturates near 0 or 1, and z-scoring by a hub SD that can be near 0 (plus 1e-9) makes the z values unstable. Both affect the head-to-head contrasts against LLM reading.
problems.fix: Count ties as one half in _shares. Use logit(p_yes) = log P(yes) - log P(no) as the LLM pair similarity. Floor the hub SD at a pre-specified quantile of the column SDs.

problems.problem: Reader-based exclusions select the benchmark for what Claude recognises. Banned positives are kept only if both Claude readers name the meme. Decoys and controls a reader thinks contain the meme are dropped. Plots are rewritten until the readers succeed. This removes exactly the hard positives and the meme-like decoys where semantic methods might fail, so the sample favours reader-like rivals (the LLM judges, embeddings) and depends on the outcome of a Claude judgement made on TEST text.
problems.fix: Pre-specify an intention-to-treat analysis on all valid stories (Q1 to Q3) as designed, ignoring Q4 and Q5, alongside the per-protocol analysis. Report exclusion rates by meme, version and writer next to every primary estimate.

problems.problem: H3 pools DEV units of three kinds, so a null cannot be interpreted. Of the 18 units, 11 are concept units, 4 are name detectors (heir, butler, losing protégé, mass breakout) and 3 are word detectors (hidden lair, coin flip, fear toxin). The name units are expected to fail in other genres, so a null H3 cannot distinguish 'concept units do not transfer' from 'name units dilute the mean'.
problems.fix: Run primary H3 on the 11 concept-class units, using the mismatched-meme null above. Pre-specify the concept-minus-name/word contrast and the all-18 result as secondary.

problems.problem: Several predictions and controls are not risky. S4 (word methods fail across languages) and S11 (keywords rank decoys above controls) are true by construction. The T1d positive control (TF-IDF with names on films that keep names) is trivial and does not show that the loose sample has any lineage signal any method can recover, so a null H5 could simply mean there is no signal. The T6 label test compares pre-filtered DEV meme-candidate neurons with randomly drawn LDA topics and clusters, and S21 has no paired test against the word-overlap floor.
problems.fix: Label S4 and S11 as construction checks rather than predictions. Add a pre-specified informativeness condition for H5: if no method, including LLM pairs and e5, recovers loose sources at p<0.05, H5 is 'uninformative'. In T6, add 40 random units drawn from all units and choose topics with a matched prevalence filter (present in 1-20% of works). Test each kind against the floor with McNemar on the same items.

problems.problem: H4 rewards being bad at level 0. In analysis.drift_interaction (line 911), D(t) = mean share at drift levels minus share at level 0, and H4 tests D_tfidf − D_neurons > 0. A method that sits at chance at every level has D ≈ 0. Section 7 makes H4 inconclusive unless TF-IDF does get worse at level 100. So whenever H4 is conclusive, a neuron method that never recovered lineage at all still 'passes'. The design was also written knowing that on DEV level 0 TF-IDF starts better (0.110 vs Qwen 0.164), which gives TF-IDF more room to degrade. A sceptic dismisses any H4 'support' as a floor effect.
problems.fix: Replace the degradation contrast with a recovery-level contrast that includes the starting level. Two options: (a) primary = the mean over levels 50, 75 and 100 of share(neurons) − share(rival), one-sided, together with a required conjunct that neurons' own lineage p < 0.05 at levels 75 and 100; or (b) the area between the recovery curve and chance, (null_mean − share) summed over all five levels, compared between methods. Keep the current D only as a descriptive curve. Add a synthetic test in test_analysis.py showing that a flat, chance-level method cannot pass.

problems.problem: The planted-story benchmark confounds meme presence with eventfulness and rewrite style, so the T2 AUCs and H3's null of 0.5 are invalid. Control fills are 'a neutral event', but every planted fill is a dramatic event. The negatives in detection_aucs (line 941) mix other plots' planted versions (about 315 of 555) with controls and decoys (about 240). A detector with no meme specificity that just fires on 'something dramatic happens' gets AUC ≈ (240 + 0.5·315)/555 ≈ 0.72 for every meme. H3 (mean AUC > 0.5, powered for 0.60) and H1 (keywords do not respond to drama) can therefore pass with no meme specificity. This repeats the mismatched-rewording flaw the robustness review found for F3, where another meme's rewording passed a unit's bar 25% of the time.
problems.fix: Before any story is written: (1) change the control fill to 'a different event of comparable dramatic weight and the same word count that is none of the 24 elements', and have the Q4 readers check this. (2) Make the primary negative set 'matched-condition': for the reworded condition, negatives = the banned and implicit versions of plots that do not plant m (same style, same wordiness, other memes) plus m's own control and decoy. (3) Replace H3's 0.5 null with a specificity null: the per-meme AUC of meme m's unit minus the mean AUC of the other memes' units on m's positives and negatives, or a permutation that shuffles detector-to-meme assignment. Report the old all-negatives AUC as secondary.

problems.problem:
The primary family does not test the organising question against vectors or LLM reading, and two of its hypotheses are nearly guaranteed to come out in the neurons' favour.
- H1: the analyst's keywords are chosen from 5 examples that use the ban-list words in nearly every sentence, and banned stories contain none of those words. Keyword AUC on reworded stories is therefore pushed towards 0.5 by construction.
- H4 and H5 use TF-IDF as the rival, although DEV already showed LSA is stronger (0.064 vs TF-IDF 0.110 vs Qwen 0.164).
- H2 is only non-inferiority against e5-base, which is about 13 times cheaper.
Even if H1 to H5 all pass, a sceptic can say that keywords failed where the design removed their words, and that embeddings would have done the same for a fraction of the cost. That does not answer 'how much more accurate or cheaper than vectors'.
problems.fix:
Restructure the primary family around the strongest rivals:
- T2: neurons vs the best pre-specified vector rival, as superiority, and vs the cached LLM judge, as an accuracy-at-cost claim.
- T1b: neurons vs LSA and vs the primary embedding at high drift.
- T1d: neurons vs LSA and vs the embedding.
- Demote H1 to a manipulation check, or rerun it against an expanded keyword query (see the keyword item).
- Add one pre-registered frontier hypothesis: on reworded T2 stories, no method is both cheaper per story at 24 memes and more accurate (AUC CI) than the neurons.
- Fix in advance how a result reads in each direction, for example 'neurons dominated by e5 means the case rests on interpretability'.
- Make neurons vs same-model hidden states a key contrast that says whether a win comes from the neuron basis or just from the model's contextual representation.

problems.problem:
Vectors are not in their strongest fair form.
(a) The encoders are dated: e5-base is primary, all-MiniLM is included, and the vector rival built on the same backbone is missing (Qwen3-Embedding 0.6B/8B, or bge-m3).
(b) T2 prototypes are positive-only means of the examples (dev_freeze line 2274). Neurons, TF-IDF keywords and LDA instead contrast against the reference-film background plus the other memes' examples.
(c) Embeddings see each sentence in isolation (readers.run_embed), while neurons and hidden states see the whole story as one continuous document. Implicit memes spread over a 1-to-3-sentence slot need that context.
(d) Lineage uses the plain cosine of mean sentence embeddings. It has no centring on the reference films (hidden states are standardised) and no alignment variant like the neurons' containment of distinctive content.
A neuron win could come from context and supervision, not from neurons.
problems.fix:
Add Qwen3-Embedding-8B (MLX or transformers) and e5-large as pre-specified vector rivals, and choose the primary encoder a priori as the strongest one, not e5-base.
- T2: give every vector method the same contrastive background. Use a contrastive prototype (mean of examples minus mean of background) and an L2 logistic probe with fixed C, plus a max-similarity-to-examples variant.
- Embed 3-sentence sliding windows and whole stories as well as single sentences.
- Lineage: centre embeddings on the reference films, and add a sentence-alignment similarity (mean over candidate sentences of the best cosine to any row sentence).
- Pick among these variants only by leave-one-example-out on the DEV examples and by DEV E2, frozen at F1, with the same number of variants for neurons (m1/m5).

problems.problem: Only the LLM methods get the meme's definition (memes_for_tracing.json: 'definition (LLM methods only)'; readers.KEYWORDS and JUDGE_QUESTION). But the stories are written from LABEL: DEFINITION, and the Q4 gate readers judge with label plus definition. Definition words that are not on the ban list (for example 'hides who they really are') will leak into banned and implicit fills. Only definition-aware methods can use that lexical channel.
problems.fix: Give every method the same inputs. Use the definition as a sixth example sentence for neuron selection, embedding prototypes, the TF-IDF query and LDA. Or run the judge in a matched no-definition arm and report both. Also extend the Q2 ban to the definition's content words, or at least report how much each banned fill overlaps with the definition.

problems.problem: There is a length confound specific to max-pooled neurons. Q1 (analysis.story_checks) matches only the number of sentences per slot, not the number of words. The drift checks (D1) do the same. Reworded or paraphrased fills are typically wordier. A unit's per-sentence max over tokens rises with sentence length for any unit, so neuron scores, and neuron presence in lineage, are inflated in banned, implicit and high-drift texts relative to controls. Mean-pooled embeddings and hidden states are much less affected. The robustness review already found length alone gives AUC 0.756 in E1.
problems.fix: Add a Q1b check that every fill of a slot is within ±15% of the explicit fill's word count, and give drift a D1b check of ±20% per sentence, with rewrite on failure. Add a 'length' pseudo-method (the story's top-3 sentence lengths; works' token counts for lineage) to every table as a floor. Pre-register a sensitivity analysis in which each unit's sentence values are residualised on log token count, using the reference-film sentences.

problems.problem:
LLM reading is handicapped in some places and leaks in others.
- Handicaps: lineage pairs read only the 150-word recursive summaries (run_pairs), never the full texts. Pairs are asked as isolated yes/no questions rather than a comparative choice. T3 likeness is read from the summary.
- Leaks: LIKENESS names 'Batman', which invokes the model's memorised knowledge of Batman, including documented influences such as Zorro and the Shadow, which are the T3 ground truth. Qwen and Llama will recognise famous name-free plots (West Side Story, Ran, Lion King 2019, Forbidden Planet) and can answer the documented 'based on' fact from memory rather than from plot similarity.
The LLM arm can look worse than it is, and better for the wrong reason.
problems.fix:
Add a full-text lineage reader. Put the candidate first as a cached prefix and use listwise scoring: all candidates' texts or summaries are cached once, and each row reads the logits over candidate letters, averaged over 2 orders. Keep the summary-based reader as the recursive-summarisation arm.
- T3: use few-shot likeness with 3 DEV Batman summaries as exemplars instead of the name 'Batman', and read full texts.
- Pre-register a recognition probe: each LLM names the title or franchise of every name-free or masked TEST text. Report T1d and T3 results for all methods both overall and on the unrecognised works.

problems.problem: The tuning budgets are unequal. The neuron lineage rule (optional band, hub adjustment, top-3 aggregation, the presence bar from the second-highest reference film) was developed on the DEV Batman E2 with forking paths: the review notes the 2-16 band and hub came after the first meme test failed. Every rival is frozen at phylo.py defaults, and the only DEV choice allowed is the hidden-state layer. T1b's Batman level 0 is those same DEV texts.

The meme set and its examples are enriched for memes the neurons already track. Eighteen of the 24 memes have a DEV-labelled Qwen unit, and the set includes all five units the review found generalise (funeral, coin flip, secret identity, joke, revenge). The definitions were broadened from DEV unit labels (for example 'Two-Face's coin' became 'coin flip'), and the examples were written with the DEV units in view. A neuron win can be dismissed as cherry-picked memes, and the sign-flip over memes generalises only to memes like these.
problems.fix: Add 8 to 12 memes drawn by a fixed seed from a neutral catalogue (the Thompson Motif Index or TV Tropes, filtered for being plantable), chosen before anyone looks at any unit, and extend planted_design.json accordingly. Have fresh agents rewrite all examples from label plus definition only, without seeing dev_units.json or DEV top sentences. Pre-register H1 and H2 on the neutral subset as a required consistency check.

problems.problem:
The keyword rival is not in its strongest fair form, and the prompts are framed unevenly.
- readers.KEYWORDS asks for 10 terms with no warning that target texts may avoid the usual words, while JUDGE_QUESTION tells the judge the element counts 'even when it is described in different words'.
- There is no expanded query of the kind an analyst who expects evasion would build: synonyms, euphemisms, WordNet or embedding neighbours.
- There is no supervised lexical classifier.
- keywords:claude is labelled an 'upper bound', but because Claude wrote the ban lists its query overlaps them most. In the banned condition it is the weakest keyword query, not the strongest.
problems.fix: Add 'keywords:expanded'. The same LLM is told 'texts may avoid the usual words; list up to 30 terms including synonyms, euphemisms and indirect indicators', and each term is expanded with WordNet synonyms. Add an L2 logistic regression on TF-IDF n-grams trained on the examples against the contrastive background. Use the expanded query as H1's rival. Report each query's overlap with the ban list. Relabel keywords:claude as 'ban-list-aligned'.

Add judge:all-memes-1pass using a cached meme-sheet prefix and teacher-forced yes/no slots read from logits. Add judge:qwen3-1.7b and a DeBERTa-v3 zero-shot NLI classifier, using the definition as the hypothesis. Report amortised setup and storage on the frontier. Compute break-even against the cheapest LLM configuration whose AUC is within the neurons' CI.

problems.problem: H5's neuron rule does not transfer. optional_band defaults to hi = n//2 over all lineage works. For T1d that is 141 films plus 40 plays, so band 2 to 90; for the drift spec it is 2 to 61. That admits near-generic units in a corpus with 40 separate sources, while the rival TF-IDF gets IDF weighting. A null H5 then reflects a band built for a single-franchise corpus of 32 works, not neurons failing, and so is uninformative.
problems.fix: Pre-specify the band relative to lineage size, for example hi = 2 × the median number of works per source + 1, or a unit-IDF-weighted containment. Make neurons-cos (reference-standardised) co-primary for H5, with a fixed rule for combining them (Holm within the pair). Validate on DEV that the new rule reproduces E2.

problems.problem: The rewording tested is synonym paraphrase, which embeddings are trained for. Mike's case is a fringe group dodging keyword moderation, which typically uses opaque coined or repurposed terms ('algospeak') whose meaning comes only from context. Neither the banned nor the drift condition tests this, so a neuron win would not show the claimed advantage, and a tie with embeddings would not refute it.
problems.fix: Add a sixth planted version, 'coded'. The meme's key concept is named by a consistent invented or repurposed term, introduced earlier in the story and defined only by context, with the ban list still enforced. Run all methods on it, and pre-register the prediction that context-using methods (neurons, hidden states, LLM) beat sentence embeddings and keywords there.

problems.problem: Recursive summarisation is a straw man on 18-to-30-sentence stories. Summarising 8-sentence chunks down to 60 words can only lose information, and S9 already predicts it loses. Recursive summarisation earns its place, and cost scaling matters most, only on long texts. Mike asked for it as a real alternative.
problems.fix: Add a long-text condition: about 20 long texts, either public-domain novels from the book family (The Scarlet Pimpernel, The Curse of Capistrano, Monte Cristo) annotated exhaustively, or 10-to-15-story concatenations with one planted meme each. On these, compare one neuron pass, the direct judge where the context allows, and recursive summarisation, on accuracy and seconds per text.

problems.problem: The ground truth and the T2 manipulation check are circular for LLM reading. Q4 admits only slots that Claude readers recognise from label plus definition. The 'Claude upper bound ≥ 0.80' check therefore passes by construction, and every LLM judge is scored against what an LLM reader recognises.
problems.fix: Add a human validation sample: Mike labels about 150 story-by-meme cells blind to version, stratified by version. Report human-Claude kappa, and make a kappa below a stated threshold an inconclusive condition. Report every method's AUC on the slots Q4 excluded as a secondary.

problems.problem: The single best unit chosen from 5 explicit examples will usually be a detector of a ban-list word (for example coin or vat), because explicit examples share those tokens. A neuron loss on banned stories is then attributable to the selection rule rather than to neurons. Equally, a sceptic of a win can point to the 884,736-feature supervised search that no rival gets.
problems.fix: Freeze at F0 a set of 5 hard-negative sentences per meme, written from the decoy hints (the keywords in a sense that does not make the meme happen), and add them to every method's contrastive background: neuron selection, TF-IDF query, LDA and the vector probes. Report m1 and m5 side by side, and pre-specify that 'single neurons are memes' is supported only if m1 is within 0.03 AUC of m5.

problems.problem: The T6 interpretability comparison is stacked. Neuron units are drawn from the 200 DEV candidate-meme units (dev_units.label_test_order), which are pre-screened for meme-likeness. LDA topics and HDBSCAN clusters are drawn at random (t6_prepare). LDA with K = 100 is fitted on single sentences, a weak form of LDA. Cluster top sentences are the ones nearest the centroid, which makes clusters easy to label. Interpretability is what the neurons fall back on if H2 fails, so this test is load-bearing.
problems.fix: Use one selection rule for every kind. Either draw at random from all units, topics or clusters present in 1% to 20% of pool works, or apply the same meme-candidate screen (enrichment in Batman works over reference films) to every kind and take the top 40. Fit LDA at work level, or on 3-sentence windows, with K = 100. Rank top sentences for every kind by its own score among members.

problems.problem:
T3 cannot show that neurons find Batman-like things better than rivals.
- S15 to S17 test neurons only against chance, and the method contrasts are two-sided with no prediction.
- The superhero centroid includes the negatives being scored (run_t3: groups['superhero'] = sup). That bias depends on dimensionality (884k units vs 768 dimensions), so it differs by method.
- The strength-A/B relatives include relations with no plot memes, such as Robin Hood (the source of Robin's name), The Man Who Laughs (the Joker's look) and Birdman (casting). These dilute every method.
problems.fix: Pre-register a directional entity-level sign-flip of neurons vs TF-IDF/LSA and vs the primary embedding on Batman-specific likeness for the relatives and the book tiers. Use leave-one-out centroids. Classify each relation in advance as plot or character versus iconography, name or meta, and test only the plot relations as primary.

problems.problem: In _shares (line 831), ties count as 'not beating' the source (strict >). A method with flat or saturated similarities, such as LLM p_yes near 1 or zero containment for a candidate with no optional units, gets z = 0 for every candidate, and then scores share 0, which counts as perfect recovery.
problems.fix: Count ties as half: share = (#others > best + 0.5·#others == best) / n. Add a unit test where a constant similarity matrix must give about 0.5.

problems.problem: Code and document disagree on summary language. translation_protocol.md says LLM readers 'write their summaries in English', but SUMMARY_CHUNK and SUMMARY_MERGE give no language instruction. Since the code wins, Chinese T1c rows may be summarised in Chinese and compared with English comic summaries.
problems.fix: Add 'Write the summary in English.' to both summary prompts, and a script check that summaries contain no CJK characters.

problems.problem: Chinese translation can bring names back in. Claude may render 'the man dressed as a bat' or a leftover name as 蝙蝠侠 or 哥谭, which multilingual encoders and Qwen read as Batman. L1 checks only Latin words and X-codes.
problems.fix: Add an L3 script check against a Chinese franchise list (蝙蝠侠, 哥谭, 韦恩, 罗宾, 阿尔弗雷德, 阿卡姆, 双面人, 猫女), with a rule that forbids standard franchise renderings in the translation prompt, and rewrite on failure.

problems.problem:
There are two drift-invariant channels, and the rewriter may echo its knowledge of Batman.
- content_types keeps only alphabetic tokens, so numbers (for example issue numbers #484 and #497 in the Knightfall comic) are never banned, yet TF-IDF tokenises them.
- X-codes survive every level and are seen by neurons, embeddings and LLMs but stripped for TF-IDF.
- Claude may recognise the work and choose replacement words that match the source comic's wording.
problems.fix: Strip digits for every method, or ban them in drift. Add a sensitivity analysis in which every X-code is replaced by one constant token for all methods. Pre-register a check on introduced words: per target, the TF-IDF similarity of the rewrite's new words (not in the original) to the documented source vs other comics, plus a sensitivity rerun with those words removed.

problems.problem: run_primary (line 2381) computes Holm over all five p-values even when a test is ruled inconclusive. A tiny p from an invalid test, such as H4 after a failed manipulation check, takes the strictest threshold and loosens the thresholds for the others.
problems.fix: Set p = 1 for any hypothesis that is inconclusive under section 7 before applying Holm, and say so in section 5.

problems.problem: T3 negatives contain Batman stories and relatives' own franchises. batman_lineage is a title regex (scratchpad scripts/t3_common.py BATMAN). That leaves about 50 superhero-stratum 'pool' negatives whose plot sections name Batman-family characters: Injustice (30 mentions), Enemies & Allies, Grayson, Justice League: Doom, Flashpoint Paradox, Gods and Monsters, Suicide Squad (2016), Birds of Prey, Teen Titans: The Judas Contract and others. Chase Me is a documented Batman work in documented_relatives.json (Wikidata P144 Batman, strength A), yet it is a pool negative. Documented relative entities also have works on both sides of the line. Superman is a strength-A relative, yet Superman II, III, IV, Returns, Man of Steel-era and animated Superman films are negatives. Two Robin Hood films are positives while 15 Robin Hood films are negatives in the same swashbuckler stratum. Darkman is a positive but Darkman II and III are negatives. The same split holds for Watchmen 2009 (positive) vs Watchmen 2024, The Phantom 1996 vs The Story of the Phantom, Dick Tracy vs Dick Tracy's Dilemma, and Iron Man 2/3 vs the Avengers films. Doctor Syn and The Spider's Web are negatives although the Pimpernel evidence sentence in the relatives file names them in Batman's lineage. Monte Cristo was excluded from negatives on the researchers' belief alone, which is asymmetric. run_t3 builds the superhero centroid from these same negatives, so 'Batman-specific likeness' has part of the Batman signal residualised away. Positives, the S14 control and every between-method contrast would all be graded against mislabelled negatives.
problems.fix: Before F0, add a rule-based 'contested' role that is excluded from negatives and from the superhero centroid, scored and reported separately. It covers (a) any pool work whose pre-mask plot or lead names a curated Batman-family character list, or whose Wikidata P674 includes one (whitelist the false hits, such as The Matrix's Bane and Lovecraft's Arkham); (b) every work of any documented relative entity at franchise level: Superman, Robin Hood, Darkman, Watchmen, Phantom, Dick Tracy, and Iron Man including the Avengers ensemble films; (c) entities named inside the evidence sentences themselves (Doctor Syn, the Spider, Green Hornet), with Monte Cristo moved under the same rule. Relabel Chase Me. Freeze the resulting counts per stratum.

problems.problem: H4 is close to guaranteed by headroom. D(t) = mean share at drift levels 25-100 minus share at level 0, with raw differences. On DEV, TF-IDF starts better than Qwen (share 0.110 vs 0.164, lower is better; chance about 0.42-0.47). Suppose both methods collapse to chance under drift: D_TF is about 0.32, D_neurons about 0.27, and H4 is 'supported' although the neurons are never better at any drift level. A sceptic dismisses a positive H4 immediately. The 14 Shakespeare clusters add a floor effect on top: loose adaptations already share few words with the plays at level 0, so they contribute about zero and dilute the test.
problems.fix: Make the primary H4 statistic a headroom-free comparison: the neurons-minus-TF-IDF difference in share at the high drift levels (mean of 75 and 100), or relative retention (chance - share_L)/(chance - share_0) with chance fixed from the permutation null. Require the interaction AND a non-negative neuron advantage at level 100 for 'supported'. Report raw degradation as secondary. Re-simulate power.

problems.problem: Drift rewrites have two confounds. (1) Authorship/style: level 0 is the original Wikipedia text, while levels 25-100 are Claude rewrites, and the candidates (comics, plays) are never rewritten. Degradation therefore mixes vocabulary loss with a switch from Wikipedia-authored to LLM-authored text, which DEV suggests matters for neurons: 3 core memes were Wikipedia house-style units. (2) Source leakage: the rewriter sees name-free but recognisable Batman and Shakespeare plots, and may choose replacement words or epithets from the source it recognises ('caped crusader', 'star-crossed', 'shrew', 'the Moor'). That raises recovery at high drift for every method and flattens the curves. D3/D4 are judged by the same model family and do not look for this. Also, the prompt says 'tell exactly the same story in different words', which invites changes beyond the banned set, so the dose at level 25 is uncontrolled.
problems.fix: (a) Add a style-only control: a fresh-session rewrite at each target with an empty ban list and the instruction to keep wording wherever possible. Report degradation relative to it, or use the slope over levels 25-100 against realised content-type survival. (b) Pre-register a source-leak index: run lineage_test with TF-IDF on introduced words only (types present in the rewrite but not the original). If it recovers sources above chance (p < 0.05), report H4 as confounded and give the sensitivity without the leaking works. (c) Change the prompt to 'replace only the listed words and whatever grammar then requires; keep every other word'. (d) Add a script check D1b: no new capitalised tokens and no franchise or play epithets (a frozen list).

problems.problem: H1 is near-tautological, and 'banned' may leave the lexical field intact. The analyst keyword queries are chosen from the same 5 explicit examples that the ban lists summarise, so keyword AUC on banned stories sits near 0.5 by construction. Meanwhile the ban checks (Q2, D2) use a light inflectional stemmer, so derivational relatives pass: avenger/avenge, killer/kill, orphanage/orphan, bribery/bribe, vengeful, funerary, vigilantism. Close synonyms are also outside many lists: memorial, wake, hearse and tomb for funeral; parents shot or killed for origin wound. Q4 then keeps only banned slots that both Claude readers recognise, which favours near-synonym rewrites. A positive H1 can be dismissed as 'synonym coverage beats a 10-word list'.
problems.fix: Freeze at F1 an expanded keyword comparator and make it H1's primary (or co-primary) rival: the LLM asked for up to 30 terms including synonyms, euphemisms and paraphrases, plus WordNet synset expansion of the TF-IDF terms. Report at F1, per meme, how much each chosen query overlaps the ban list. In Q2 and D2, ban derivational families (shared-prefix match on stems of 5 or more letters, plus a frozen family list). Pre-register a lexical-residue measure for banned and implicit slots (share containing an expanded-synonym term) and report AUC split by residue.

problems.problem: The frame leaks context into the all-negatives AUC. One writer call, which knows the 3 memes, writes the frame and all 5 fills. So the frame carries each meme's setting (wealthy family, constables, a ranch to inherit) in every version, including the control. H1-H3 use positives (reworded versions) against about 555 negatives, mostly from other plots without that setting. A method that detects topical context (embeddings, neurons, LDA) earns AUC from the frame, not the planted slot. This is exactly the shared-topic reading a sceptic will offer.
problems.fix: Make the primary H1-H3 statistic within-plot: the hard-negative AUC (reworded versions vs. the same plot's control and decoy), or a plot-stratified AUC or conditional-logit contrast. Keep the all-negatives AUC as secondary. Recompute power with about 15 within-plot pairs per meme.

problems.problem: Validation is a single-model monoculture, and the main manipulation check is circular. Claude writes the stories, ban lists, examples, translations, drift rewrites and name removals. It also runs the blind reads, back-translation, the L2/D3/N3 checks, T2-N annotation, adjudication and the label test. Kappa between two Claude sessions measures one rater's test-retest consistency, not inter-annotator reliability. The H1-H3 validity check (Claude upper-bound reworded AUC of at least 0.80) is run on stories already filtered by Claude readers, so it passes by selection. Back-translation by Claude can rebuild a known plot from memory, so L2 is lenient. Q4 readers pick from a menu of 24 definitions, which is easier than recall.
problems.fix: Add a second reader from a different model family that is not a method (for example GPT- or Gemini-class through an API, or a local open model such as Gemma or Mistral that fits in 24 GB) for Q4/Q5, A2, D3 and L2, and report cross-family agreement. Add a human audit by Mike of a stratified random sample: about 40 banned/implicit slots, 20 controls/decoys, 10 T2-N works and 20 drift and translation pairs. Pre-register pass thresholds, for example at least 85% presence agreement on banned/implicit slots and at least 95% absence on controls. Replace the Claude-upper-bound check with the cross-family and human audit. Do the back-translation with Qwen MT or another model family.

problems.problem: The 5 'name-free, varied-setting' examples per meme are close paraphrases of Batman, Zorro and Pimpernel scenes. Examples include: 'Knowing that criminals are a superstitious lot, he designs a frightening costume'; falls into a vat of chemicals 'with bleached white skin' or 'green hair and a frozen smile'; a joke card left at every crime scene; holding a pistol to a man's head while 'only the coin will decide'; a lazy fop 'yawning through council meetings'; a hidden cave beneath the manor; a family butler who raises the orphan. DEV Batman texts contain 'vat of chemicals', 'bleached', 'chemical plant', 'green hair', 'fear toxin' (8 sentences), 'antidote' (8) and 'butler' (7), which are absent or rare in the 69 reference films. These examples define every method's detector in T2-N (Batman lineage and relatives) and in T3's orphan-vigilante layer. T2-N then measures recall of Batman sentences rather than tracking under natural wording, and S16 (Zorro, Pimpernel and Iron Man score high on Tier A) is circular.
problems.fix: Before F0, write a second 'far' example set blind: an agent given only the definition, forbidden from crime cities, colonial California, revolutionary France, billionaire inventors and costumed avengers. Screen it so that each example's maximum TF-IDF and e5 cosine to DEV Batman and cousin sentences is no higher than its maximum to reference-film sentences. Pre-register the far set as primary for T2-N and T3, keep the current set for planted T2, and report both.

problems.problem: The meme inventory was chosen with the neurons in view. 18 of the 24 memes come from DEV-labelled Qwen units. 6 of those units (origin wound, secret identity, losing the protégé, the joke, funeral, coin flip) already passed DEV's rewording test (results/wording.json). Llama's H3 revenge unit was picked from 50 for winning DEV minimal pairs. H1-H3 average over memes for which the neurons are known to have clean units, so a sceptic will say the benchmark was selected for neuron-detectability.
problems.fix: Add 10-12 motifs drawn by seed from an external index (Thompson Motif-Index, ATU or a TV Tropes plot index), filtered only for being expressible in a plot summary. Write their definitions, examples and ban lists under the same protocol before F0. Include them in H1/H2, or run the same tests on them as a co-reported stratum. Split H3 by DEV-rewording survivors vs non-survivors and by DEV class (concept vs name units such as heir_to_fortune and butler_raised_him). Say plainly that the Llama revenge unit was chosen on DEV.

problems.problem: The Shakespeare ground truth is weaker than H5 assumes. 27 of the 83 loose films are documented only by a 'Films based on X' category (17 of Romeo and Juliet's 32), for example Ex Machina as The Tempest, Kentucky (1938) as Romeo and Juliet, and Jubal as Othello. Such categories are often added because the plot looks similar, which is circular, and wrong ones make a null uninformative. 'Loose' means only that fewer than 2 principal names appear in the summary, so short or vague summaries of faithful films count as loose; it does not measure changed wording or setting. The Lion King (2019), The Lion King 1½ and The Lion King II are flagged remake_of_dev but stay in H5; The Lion King 1½'s Hamlet link is second-order. 21 of the 40 plays are cut to their first 40 sentences (Macbeth 64, King Lear 54, Othello 48, Hamlet 45, Midsummer 72, Troilus 127), which drops the endings that adaptations keep. Four plays enter the play-weighted mean with a single film each.
problems.fix: Pre-register evidence tiers and make H5's primary sample the loose films with a lead-sentence or Wikidata P144 source (56 films, 13 plays), with category-only films as a sensitivity. Drop the remake_of_dev films from H5. Add a blind, lead-based judgement of setting change (from the lead, not the plot) to the loose definition, or rename the sample 'renamed adaptations'. Use full play synopses (or 40 sentences sampled evenly) instead of head truncation, and remove commentary sections (Measure for Measure's 'Synopsis and themes'). Report results with single-film plays dropped.

problems.problem: The T3 relatives ground truth mixes relations that plot summaries cannot show, and much of it is not fresh. Several T3 positives are iconography- or name-only influences: the Joker's face (The Man Who Laughs), Robin's name (Robin Hood), white eye lenses (The Phantom), Iron Man's armour collection, and Birdman's casting meta-references. Puss in Boots is a Batman 'sibling' only through Zorro. Strength A is inflated by crowd-edited Wikidata links (Birdman 'based on' Batman). Jerry Warren's Batwoman (1966) is a documented derivative but is labelled batman_lineage by the title regex. The entities were ascertained from a hand-picked article list (relatives_wp.py) chosen from prior belief. Zorro, Pimpernel, Iron Man, Spider-Man, Shadow, Bat, Holmes and Superman all have DEV cousins whose E1 scores are known. Their TEST works are mostly remakes and sequels of those DEV works (Pimpernel 1934/1982, Mark of Zorro 1974, Iron Man 2/3), so S15-S17 are partly predicted from DEV.
problems.fix: Before F0, have two blind coders type each relation as plot/role-level, iconography/name-only, parody/pastiche, meta or transitive. Make S15's primary set the plot/role-level relations plus parodies, and report iconography-only relations separately with a predicted null. Split entities into DEV-franchise and franchise-fresh (Doc Savage, Dick Tracy, Darkman, Watchmen, parodies and others), make the fresh set confirmatory, and write the known DEV cousin values into the prereg. Relabel Batwoman 1966 (and Batman XXX, The People's Joker and Catwoman 2004, which has no Batman connection) as derivatives, or exclude them from the lineage.

problems.problem: T3 permutation inference treats works as independent. stratified_perm_test moves positive labels across individual works within strata, so under the null Zorro's 18 near-duplicate retellings become 18 independent random works. The real Zorro contribution behaves like about one story, so the null is too narrow and p-values are anti-conservative.
