S16 and S17 each rest on 3 entities (Zorro, Pimpernel, Iron Man; Spider-Man, John Wick, Puss in Boots). The pool negatives are clustered too (about 20 Superman films, 15 Robin Hood films, 13 Justice League films). Category priority also puts 12 of 18 Zorro films in the superhero stratum rather than the swashbuckler stratum.
problems.fix: Use an entity-level test: compare each entity's mean AUC against pseudo-entities built from franchise clusters of pool negatives (grouped by Wikidata P179/P144 or title stem, size-matched), or use a sign test over entities. Report the number of entities and present S16/S17 as descriptive estimates with n = 3. Assign strata by a frozen rule based on the work's own genre (lead/shortdesc) rather than category-crawl priority, and report sensitivity to it.

problems.problem: The design of T2-N (natural-text meme tracing) limits what it can show. It annotates only the 120 Batman-lineage, relative and book-family works. Tier A memes are therefore near-ubiquitous and have few negatives. The 'at least 3 positives' rule has no matching minimum for negatives. Claude annotators will recognise masked Batman and Zorro works and can label canonical memes from memory rather than from the sentence. This is the only test of meme tracing in human-written text, and as designed it can neither support nor refute 'tracking a meme when the words change'.
problems.fix: Add 100-150 seeded random pool works (random, superhero and pulp strata, excluding contested ones) to the annotated set, so that natural positives (funerals, revenge vows, twins, coin flips) and negatives occur outside Batman. Require at least 10 positives and 10 negatives per meme. Require each annotation to quote its evidence span, with the instruction 'judge only from the text, not from what you know of the work'. Set a minimum kappa for inclusion in the mean (for example 0.4). Use the far example set, and include T2-N in the human audit.

problems.problem: T4 (mutation and selection) is confounded by the sample. 42 of the 43 TEST lineage works are from 1995 or later. The one 1966 TEST work is Jerry Warren's Batwoman knock-off, not Batman, so the 1966-1986 gap is unchanged. Three of the 7 fresh adaptations retell the predicted innovators (Year One 2011, The Dark Knight Returns 2012, The Killing Joke 2016), so S18's 'mutations that catch on' are largely heredity through direct adaptation. The DEV name-free texts came from batched rewrites (data/anon/batch_*.jsonl) under a different procedure from the new one-work-per-session protocol. Any processing batch effect appears as 'mutations' first seen in the earliest TEST-processed work and 'inherited' by every later TEST work.
problems.fix: Re-run name removal on all 75 works with the new protocol in one pass for T4 (keep the old DEV texts for the DEV comparisons). Pre-register a batch-effect check: a classifier separating DEV- from TEST-processed works within 1995-2022 on unit presence; flag T4 if its AUC exceeds 0.7. When computing a work's success, exclude its documented adaptations, in both the observed and the shuffled orders. Relabel Batwoman 1966. State that TEST adds no work before 1995.

problems.problem: X-codes can give the neurons a cue that the word methods are denied. TF-IDF and word presence strip codes, but the neurons see X1...Xn: cast size, how dense the codes are, and which code numbers appear where. In T1c the codes are the only tokens shared between the Chinese targets and the English comics. A neuron win in H5 or S3 could come from cast structure rather than plot memes.
problems.fix: At F1, run a codes-only baseline on DEV E2: per-work features such as the number of distinct codes, codes per sentence and the positional code profile, put through lineage_test. Run the same baseline on every TEST lineage set. If it beats chance on DEV, pre-register a code-collapsed sensitivity (every code replaced by one neutral token for all methods) for H5 and T1c, and report it beside the primary result.

problems.problem: The translation checks cannot catch re-canonicalisation or translationese. In T2-zh, a translator may render an English paraphrase back into the canonical Chinese term (a 'self-appointed avenger' becomes 义警, vigilante), which the Qwen-translated keyword queries then hit. The banned Chinese stories are never checked against a Chinese ban list. Translation is forced sentence by sentence, so the texts keep English structure. T1c therefore tests machine-translated Chinese, not Chinese text.
problems.fix: Translate each ban list into Chinese with two translators plus a dictionary, require banned and control zh stories to contain none of those terms (L3 check, re-translate once, then flag), and report. Add a natural cross-language arm: the zh.wikipedia plot sections of the Batman screen works that have them, which are written independently. Run them through the same name-removal protocol in Chinese, and frame T1c's agent-translated result as 'machine-translated Chinese'.

problems.problem: Planted-story labels are asymmetric. A version is excluded for an unplanted meme only when both readers name it (Q5), so single-reader detections stay as negatives. An implicit positive needs only one reader. LLM judges that correctly flag a naturally occurring funeral or inheritance in a frame are penalised, and label noise lowers every AUC unevenly across methods.
problems.fix: Make the rule symmetric. A story is a negative for meme m only if no reader names m. A single-reader flag is excluded or sent to a third, cross-family reader. Report how many cells the rule changes.

problems.problem: Drift is not compared with consistent references, and the dose is unobserved. Presence bars for drifted texts come from undrifted reference films, whereas T1c translates its reference films, an inconsistent choice. The x-axis is the nominal level rather than the realised replacement.
problems.fix: Drift the 69 reference films at each level (276 extra rewrites) as a sensitivity, or justify the undrifted bars as the realistic analyst's choice and say so. Plot recovery against realised content-type survival (D2), and pre-register a minimum spacing between levels (for example, at least 15 points of survival between adjacent levels on average), or else report the levels as merged.

problems.problem: Plot texts can still state the relation or leak names. Some positives' plot sections state the relation outright, for example '(a parody of Batman and Robin)' in the Bluntman plot and '(a parody of Batman)' for Commander Courage, and after masking a cue such as 'a parody of X' remains. The capitalisation masker misses sentence-initial names that never recur mid-sentence (129 such misses on DEV), so a literal 'Batman' can survive in a pool negative and favour the keyword and LLM methods.
problems.fix: Before masking, remove by a frozen rule any parenthetical or sentence containing 'parody of', 'based on', 'inspired by', 'homage to' or 'pastiche'. Apply it to all T3 works alike. After masking, scan with analysis.FRANCHISE, mask any hits and report the counts.

problems.problem: Wikipedia editors sometimes copy plot sentences between an adaptation's article and its source's article (common for DC animated adaptations). The Batman lineage signal at level 0, and T1e, may then rest on verbatim reuse rather than inherited content.
problems.fix: Pre-register a reuse audit: shared 8-grams between each target and its documented source and other candidates. Report it, and run H4's Batman arm and T1e without sentences that share an 8-gram with any candidate.

problems.problem: The T6 label-test selection favours neurons. The 40 neuron units come from DEV meme-candidate units restricted to 1-20% pool presence, while the LDA topics and HDBSCAN clusters are drawn at random with no matching frequency filter. HDBSCAN's held-out sentences are near-centroid, which also makes clusters easy to label.
problems.fix: Run two arms with matched selection. (a) Random: neuron units drawn at random from all units with 1-20% work-level presence; topics and clusters filtered to the same work-level presence band. (b) Best-of: each method's top 40 by its own quality score (DEV meme score, topic coherence, cluster persistence). Report both.

problems.problem: The TEST source texts exist only in the session scratchpad, which the OS can delete. preregistration/build_lists.py hard-codes SCOUT and ROBUST to <scratchpad>/prereg/scout and .../robust. stage_wikipedia() reads every Shakespeare, T3-pool, relative and new-Batman plot section from those caches (126 MB), and the pre-registration commits only their sha256 hashes. macOS clears /private/tmp at boot and periodically, and the scratchpad is tied to this session. Wikipedia has already been edited since 2026-10-20, so re-fetching would fail every frozen-hash assert. T1d, T1e, T3, T4 and T2-N could then not be built as frozen, and no outsider could rebuild F2 from the public repo.
problems.fix: Before F0, copy the scout caches into the project: plays.jsonl, films_all.jsonl, t3/candidates.jsonl, t3/random_films.jsonl, relatives/works.jsonl, and any ROBUST file build_lists reads. Put them under, for example, prereg/sources/, committed or as a hashed tarball, with a CC BY-SA attribution line in DATA_LICENSE.md. Make SCOUT and ROBUST relative paths. Rerun `build_lists.py lists`, confirm every hash is unchanged, and commit. Copying the files computes no outcome.

problems.problem: H4 is biased toward neurons by its starting points. The statistic is degradation D = mean share at drift levels 25-100 minus share at level 0, and shares are bounded above by chance (about 0.45), so a method that starts better has more room to degrade. On DEV, TF-IDF starts at 0.110 and Qwen at 0.164. If both collapse to chance under heavy drift, D_tfidf - D_neurons comes out at about +0.04 to +0.05 even though neither method is more robust. That is half the 0.10 effect H4 is powered for, so a sceptic can dismiss a supported H4 as a floor artefact. test_analysis.py never checks the case where both methods collapse.
problems.fix: Make the primary H4 statistic a direct comparison under drift: the mean over levels 50, 75 and 100 of share(neurons) - share(TF-IDF), one-sided, using the same cluster sign-flip. Alternatively, use headroom-normalised retention, (null_mean_t - share_t,L) / (null_mean_t - share_t,0), with each target's null mean taken from the permutation null. Report the level-0 difference next to it. Add a synthetic test in which both methods fall to chance, and require the statistic to be about 0 with p ≥ 0.05.

problems.problem: H1 is won by construction, so a positive result says little. The ban lists strip each meme's usual words from the banned, implicit and control stories, and Qwen's frozen analyst queries are built from those same words. I checked the frozen inputs: in /private/tmp/.../scratchpad/prereg/readercheck/features/t2_examples/keywords_qwen3-8b.json, 204 of 205 Qwen terms are multi-word phrases, and 183 of 205 contain a banned stem. Under the all-stems matching rule those 183 can never fire in a banned story. The 22 that can are phrases like 'lawbreaker with means' or 'funny execution', which need every stem in one sentence. Keyword AUC on reworded stories will therefore be about 0.5 with ties, and H1 collapses into 'neurons > 0.5', which is nearly H3. The budgets are also lopsided: the keyword analyst gets one 1-second call with no feedback, while neurons search 884,736 units against a contrastive background.
problems.fix: Publish the overlap between each query and its ban list now; it uses only frozen inputs. Replace H1's comparator with an evasion-aware keyword analyst on a matched budget, using a frozen prompt: 30 to 50 mostly single-word terms including synonyms, euphemisms and paraphrase vocabulary, after the analyst has seen its query's hit counts on the 5 examples and on the DEV background and revised once. Keep the current query as a secondary. Add an 'update' arm that models moderation under evasion: both keywords and neurons receive 5 banned-condition example sentences from a held-out set of plots and re-select. Report accuracy and the cost of each update.

problems.problem: Supervision and tuning budgets differ between methods, which breaks the 'identical tuning budget' rule. Neurons m1 runs a contrastive search over 884,736 units, using percentile ranks against the 2,267 background sentences plus the other memes' examples. Embeddings and hidden states get a plain mean prototype with no contrast, LDA picks the best of 50 topics, and the topic model takes the nearest cluster. In T1, the neuron rule (2-16 band, hub z-scores, top-3 pooling) was refined on DEV over several iterations: per the robustness verdict, the band and hub came after the first meme-Jaccard test failed. The rivals run on defaults. A positive H2, or a win over vectors in T1 or T2, can be dismissed as extra supervision and tuning rather than a better representation.
problems.fix: At F1, give every vector rival the same contrastive supervision: a difference-of-means direction, or an L2 logistic regression on the 5 examples against the same contrastive background, for e5 and hidden states. For lineage, also run the rivals through the neuron rule where it is defined: top-3 sentence pooling for embeddings, and presence of embedding dimensions or topics via the same reference-film bar, the same band and the same containment. Choose rival hyperparameters on DEV E2 from a stated grid at least as large as the number of rule variants the neuron pipeline tried on DEV, and freeze them at F1. Report the selection compute as setup cost.

problems.problem: The LLM judge is not run in its cheapest reasonable setup, and the break-even figure is degenerate. Its per-meme cost of 0.2 s comes from repeating the label, definition and 5 examples (about 200 tokens) after every story. The scout measured 0.12 s per meme without the examples. Caching all 24 memes' definitions and examples once as a prefix, then reading the story and asking 24 short questions (about 10 tokens each), would cut the per-meme cost roughly tenfold. LLM reading would then cost about 2x the neuron pass per story at 24 memes, not about 14x. Separately, the neuron pass and the judge's prefill are the same forward pass (0.355 s vs 0.362 s in /private/tmp/.../scout/tools/neuron_timing_qwen3-8b.json and llm_timing_qwen3-8b.json), so M* = (neuron - prefill) / per_meme is about 0 whatever the configuration. The synthetic test already returns 0.0. Any 'neurons are N times cheaper than LLM reading' claim therefore depends on an unchosen implementation.
problems.fix: Add a frozen `judge-shared:<model>` variant to readers.py (memes-first cached prefix, short per-meme questions) and report its accuracy and cost alongside the current judge. Replace M* with total-cost curves C(N stories, M memes, Q later queries) for every method, including setup. State plainly that the neuron pass equals a judge prefill, so the neurons' cost advantage over LLM reading is only the per-meme term, and that embeddings and keywords also score every meme from a single pass.

problems.problem: The cost accounting is inconsistent, and parts of section 9 are not implemented. (a) readers.run_embed starts its timer before the encoder loads; the MLX timers exclude model loading. (b) The TEST extractions run with --hidden, so hidden-state capture and per-sentence writes are charged to neurons in both seconds and bytes (meta['bytes'] sums every .npy), while the hidden rival is charged nothing. (c) Peak memory is mx.get_peak_memory (the GPU allocator) for MLX but ru_maxrss (CPU RSS) for torch, so the figures are not comparable. (d) The one-off costs section 9 promises are never timed: dev_freeze has no timers. select_units re-sorts the 2,387 x 884,736 background once for each of the 24 memes, about a minute per meme per model; that is the true per-new-meme setup cost of neurons, against about 1 s for keywords and microseconds for an embedding prototype. Also untimed: the 4 GB of full background activations per model, reference-film extraction per text condition, and the roughly 207 Claude calls to translate 69 films that only the neuron and words presence bars need. (e) Composite methods have no cost recipe: summary-judge (summaries plus judge), LLM lineage (summaries of rows and candidates plus pairs), and MT plus TF-IDF. No frontier is computed anywhere in analysis.py. (f) Timings come from production runs on a shared laptop; another workflow is active now. Section 9 says conflicting jobs are logged, but no code does this, and the first, cold call costs about twice a warm one (0.70 s vs 0.36 s).
problems.fix: Before F0, add a frozen bench.py. It runs each method on fixed subsets after a warm-up, with 3 repeats and nothing else running, and records os.getloadavg() and the running python and MLX processes in every cost JSON. Measure memory the same way for every method, for example /usr/bin/time -l max RSS plus the MLX peak, and record load time separately. Time a neurons-only pass without --hidden. Put timers on every dev_freeze step, and cache the sorted background once. Charge reference-corpus, translation and labelling setup to the methods that need them. Write the per-method cost recipes and the frontier formula into analysis.run_cost.

problems.problem: The agent budget is undercounted by roughly 1.6 to 1.9x, and no generation protocol has been piloted. Blind reads alone are 600 versions x 2 = 1,200 calls, plus 120 writer calls, but the budget lists 600 for stories and reads together. The label test needs about 16 labeller calls and 160 units x 2 items x 2 judges = 640 judge calls; the budget lists 40. Drift repairs will exceed the ~50 assumed: level 100 bans every content type in the original, and D2 must be empty. A realistic total is 5,000 to 6,500 fresh Claude sessions, not 3,400, with no token, wall-clock or money estimate. Failure rates are unknown under the strict Q2 rule, the both-readers Q4 rule, Q5 contamination and 15 fills per plot. A meme is dropped once more than 4 of its 15 plots fail, so H1 to H3 can lose memes and power, which would leave a null uninformative. A single freeze at F2 also means one stalled data stream blocks every test.
problems.fix: Recount the budget and add tokens, wall-clock time and cost. Before F0, run a labelled PILOT that is excluded from TEST: about 6 planted plots, 2 DEV reference films drifted at levels 50 and 100, and 3 translations. Use it to measure Q1-Q5, D1-D4 and L1-L2 pass rates and calls per item, and fix the protocols on that basis. Pre-specify a minimum viable completion for each test. Use staged freezes (F2-T2, F2-T1b, F2-T1c/d, F2-T3), each committed and pushed before that test's methods run.

problems.problem: Neuron units for T2 are selected in a different context from the one they are scored in. They are selected and standardised on one-sentence documents after a fixed prefix (t2_examples and t2_background with --prefix), but scored on sentences inside continuous stories of 18 to 30 sentences. SwiGLU channel activations shift with position and context; sentence embeddings have no such mismatch. If H1 to H3 come out null, a defender can blame the selection protocol rather than the representation, so the null cannot settle the question.
problems.fix: Before F1, check on DEV that the chosen units' single-sentence activations predict their in-context activations. dev_original is already extracted in context and t2_background as single sentences, so the per-unit rank correlation for selected units costs nothing. Pre-specify a secondary that selects against in-context background (the reference films as whole documents, with each example embedded in a fixed neutral DEV paragraph), and report both.

problems.problem: Recursive summarisation is tested outside the conditions it is meant for. Every text is at most 40 sentences (about 1,200 tokens) and fits in the context window, so the 150-word summary can only lose information while adding about 6.5 s per story. LLM lineage reading is given only the two summaries, while neurons see the full text. A neuron win over LLM reading on T1 can be dismissed as beating a starved reader.
problems.fix: Add full-text pairwise reading on a pre-specified subset, caching each candidate's prefix: Batman at levels 0 and 100 (16 targets x 12 comics x 2 levels = 384 pairs) and the loose Shakespeare films at level 0 (83 x 40 = 3,320 pairs), about 1 to 2 hours per model. State the scope plainly: the accuracy and cost results apply to summaries of 40 sentences or fewer, and the long-text case where recursive summarisation would matter is not tested.

problems.problem: The neuron advantage of 'one pass, any future meme' rests on storing every unit's aggregate, at 1.8 MB per work in fp16 (about 1.8 TB per million works). Embeddings have the same property at about 1.5 KB per work for a mean vector, roughly 1,000x less. Section 9 reports storage per work only as produced, and that figure is inflated by hidden.npy and sent.npy.
problems.fix: Report storage and re-scoring cost under three retention policies: all units, selected units only, and no storage (re-extract when needed). Say explicitly in the cost section that the one-pass, every-meme property is shared by embeddings and keywords.

problems.problem: The human-effort claim cannot be tested as designed. Every method gets the same 5 examples, and the analyst's keyword choice is an automated 1-second LLM call, so the design cannot show that neurons save human effort compared with keywords. Making neuron memes nameable, which Mike's goals 1 and 4 need, requires agent labelling. That cost is not charged to neurons: H3's DEV labels came from the earlier pipeline at an uncounted cost, T6 labels only 40 units, and DEV had 14,843 families. LDA and the topic model get c-TF-IDF labels at no cost.
problems.fix: Count the labelling calls behind the H3 DEV units from the earlier run's logs. In T6, report calls per usable, non-'unclear' label, and extrapolate to the number of units needed to cover the T3 pool. State the effort claim narrowly: in this design the only effort neurons save over keywords is the keyword-choice call.

problems.problem: Resuming an interrupted extraction can silently mix stale rows into a rebuilt set. extract_compact.py reopens an existing agg/sent/full/hidden.npy in r+ mode, which keeps the old shape. Rows are addressed by work index, and progress.json skips by id. If a set file changes, for example after a repair or a bug fix, old rows survive without any error.
problems.fix: Store the set file's sha256 and n_works in progress.json and meta.json, and abort on any mismatch unless --fresh is given, which deletes the old arrays.

problems.problem: 21 of the 40 Shakespeare plays hit the 40-sentence cap (works_shakespeare.json, n_sentences = 40), so their endings are cut from the source texts. That lowers the signal for every method in T1d and H5, making a null less informative. Restoring the full texts would cost about a minute of extraction plus a few summary chunks.
problems.fix: Before F0, decide to use the plays uncapped, or capped at 80 sentences, as candidates; they are already in the scout cache. Re-hash them, and report how many films are truncated.

problems.problem: Drift effort is concentrated where it adds little to H4. Romeo and Juliet supplies 32 of the 83 loose films, so it takes about 256 of the roughly 660 Shakespeare drift agent calls, yet it counts as only 1 of H4's 30 equally weighted clusters.
problems.fix: Cap drifted films at about 6 per play, chosen in sha256 order. This saves about 200 agent calls with negligible loss of power. The cap applies to T1b only; H5 still uses all 83 loose films.

problems.problem: In T3, the LLM likeness method gets different inputs from every other method. It asks whether a story is 'like the Batman stories', drawing on the model's prior knowledge plus whatever names leak through the deterministic masker's roughly 9% misses. The other methods only see the centroid of the 32 DEV works. This breaks the identical-inputs rule.
problems.fix: Give the LLM the same reference, for example the merged recursive summary of the 32 DEV Batman works in the prompt. Alternatively, label the method as 'different input: prior knowledge' wherever it appears in a contrast.

problems.problem: Several budget figures come from made-up text rather than DEV measurements. devcheck measured about 38 sentences per second with --hidden (90 sentences in 2.36 s), not 68, so extraction takes about 1 hour per model, not 35 minutes. The brief's figure of 3,700 sentences per 12 minutes, which applies to the old extractor, is never reconciled. e5-base was measured at 443 sentences per second at 64 tokens, against the 900 claimed. The 27 GPU-hours of LLM time ignore laptop thermal throttling.
problems.fix: Rebuild section 11 from the DEV-measured rates, explain why the compact extractor is about 7x faster than extract.py, and record wall-clock time per batch so that any throttling shows up in the cost tables.

changes_made: BLOCKER (all 4 reviews), H4 floor effect: replaced the degradation statistic with a head-to-head at drift levels 50-100 (share(rival) - share(neurons)), intersection-union over TF-IDF and LSA, with a required conjunct that the neurons' own pooled lineage test is p<0.05 at levels 75 and 100 (analysis.h4_head_to_head, pooled_lineage). Null worlds: equal robustness with the DEV gap rejects 0.000 (draft 0.185); total loss 0.055 (draft 0.465). Headroom-free retention (each target's own null mean) is secondary; draft statistic descriptive only. Batman targets clustered by first-listed source comic (8) + 13 plays = 21 clusters; connected-components clustering as sensitivity.

BLOCKER, T2 eventfulness and frame confounds: control fills are now 'an event of equal stakes and dramatic weight' with blind salience ratings (Q6); primary detection is within-plot 'twin AUC' (planted story vs its own plot's control, identical frame); matched-condition, all-negatives, hard and decoy schemes secondary; non-specific detector scores 0.50 in the null world (draft rule 0.59). H3 is now a specificity test on the 11 DEV concept units with a mismatched-meme permutation null (null rejection 0.000).

BLOCKER, H1 rigged keyword rival: H1 rivals are an evasion-aware LLM analyst (30-40 mostly single-word terms, one revision after seeing hit counts on examples and DEV background, WordNet expansion) and an L2 lexical probe (keywords:logreg), intersection-union; decoys removed from primary negatives; per-query ban-list overlap published at F1. Draft Qwen queries measured: 203/205 multi-word, mean ban-list overlap 0.90, only 23 terms could fire in a banned story.

BLOCKER, T3 contamination: rule-based 'contested' role (115 works: Batman-family names in pre-mask plot/lead, franchise works of T3-positive entities incl. Superman, Robin Hood, Darkman, Watchmen, Phantom, Dick Tracy, Iron Man/Avengers, Holmes, Shadow, Bat, Doc Savage; heroes named in evidence sentences: Doctor Syn, the Spider, Green Hornet); 4 lineage titles relabelled (Wild World of Batwoman -> relative; Batman XXX, The People's Joker, Catwoman 2004 -> contested); Chase Me contested; Monte Cristo moved to pool and reported descriptively.

BLOCKER, scratchpad-only sources: copied gzipped scout caches and the needed robustness files into prereg/sources/ (9.4 MB) with a CC BY-SA licence file; build_lists.py now reads only project files; per-work hashes of films and pool works verified unchanged.

Primary family restructured around the strongest rivals: H1 (evasion-aware keywords + lexical probe), H2 (non-inferiority then superiority vs Qwen3-Embedding-4B sentences, Qwen3-Embedding-4B 3-sentence windows, e5-large), H3 (specificity), H4 (vs TF-IDF and LSA), H5 (vs TF-IDF and LSA), plus H6 frontier decision rule (no method at least as accurate and no more expensive per story at 34 memes). Interpretation of each outcome fixed in advance (section 1.5).

Three-way verdicts with smallest effects of interest (0.05 AUC / 0.05 share): supported (Holm rejects + required conditions), falsified (one-sided falsification test excludes SESOI), undetermined, inconclusive; inconclusive hypotheses enter Holm with p = 1; H5 can be 'uninformative'. Realistic power re-simulated (history/power_sim_v2.py).

Lineage null made time-consistent (rejection sampling of relabellings) with a unit test against exact enumeration; ties count one half; LLM pair similarity uses logit; hub SD floored at the 10th percentile; per-target null means returned.

Equal supervision and tuning budget: every family gets definition + explicit + reworded examples and the same contrastive background (reference sentences, other memes' sentences, own hard negatives); two variants per T2 family chosen by leave-one-example-out (neurons m1/m5; embeddings and hidden states contrastive prototype/probe; LDA K 50/100); lineage grid of at most 4 configurations per family chosen on DEV E2 at F1 (neurons base/idf/quarter-band/cos; TF-IDF variants; LSA k; LDA K; embeddings mean/centred/alignment/neuron-rule presence; hidden layer; topic min_cluster_size). One-pass neuron detector selection with LOEO (analysis.neuron_detectors).

Meme set and examples: 10 neutral motifs drawn by seed from five Wikipedia motif/plot categories with a documented plantability walk (34 memes, Tier N); all example sets (explicit, reworded, far, hard_negative) to be rewritten blind by fresh agents at step P1 with script and reader screens (build_lists.py texts examples, analysis.far_screen_tfidf, F1 e5 screen); neutral-subset consistency required for H1/H2; far set used for T2-N and T3.

Planted design rebuilt: 136 plots x 6 versions (new 'coded' version: invented/repurposed term understood only from context) = 816 stories; 17 genres, 4 writers; each meme in 12 plots; Q1b length matching (+/-15%), derivational ban rule (analysis.ban_hits: 5-letter shared prefix + frozen families), symmetric Q5, cross-family reader (Gemma 2 9B), salience ratings, ITT analysis, meme-drop rule implemented (>3 of 12 plots), T2-long (48 concatenated long texts).

Inference dependence: H1/H2 must pass both meme-level and plot-level sign flips (analysis.plot_flip_test) after a null world showed shared plots inflate rejection to 0.105 (now 0.03); two-way meme x plot bootstrap, per-writer and leave-one-writer-out estimates.

Vectors strengthened: Qwen3-Embedding-4B (pinned) as primary, 3-sentence windows and whole-document embeddings, centred/alignment/presence lineage variants, contrastive probes; neurons vs same-model hidden states as key contrast.

GPT or Gemini as the second reader family (review 3): no API access is set up and stories would leave the machine; a local Gemma 2 9B (fallback Mistral 7B) is used.
